title: 3. Conditional PPO fallback: does reward optimization yield a usable expert?
hypothesis: On-policy PPO learns state-dependent multi-finger coordination that sustains axial rolling on stages where the frozen scripted controllers cannot qualify.

prediction.rationale: Comparator is the frozen R-039 feedback gait (D-035: 14/30, 16/30, 7/30 sustained on its promotion cases). Reported separately per stage on 30 fresh paired cases (seeds 4030-4032); one Stage-3-trained policy is scored on all three stages because the predicates nest.

protocol.command: gpu run 'source ~/IsaacLab/source_env.sh && python scripts/isaac/train_pen_spin_expert.py --config config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml --research-protocol ppo_expert'
code_changes: Add scripts/isaac/train_pen_spin_expert.py: rsl_rl OnPolicyRunner on the vendored Stage-3 env (lares.envs.isaac_pen_spin) with the vendored ShadowHandSpinPPORunnerCfg, training seed 4020, the existing Stage-3 reward unchanged. One policy for all stages: the stages share physics and their per-step predicates nest (Stage-3 success implies Stage-1/2 success on the same trajectory).

Schedule predeclared: up to 1.08e9 environment transitions; target 8192 parallel envs; a throughput/memory gate in the first segment freezes the largest feasible env count before continuing; fixed checkpoints every 10% of the schedule; the final scheduled checkpoint is the only one evaluated. No checkpoint selection, extension or reward change from promotion outcomes.

Diagnostics at each checkpoint from training rollouts, logged separately from return: reward components (spin, centre, axis, action), axial roll rate, end-over-end rate, fall frequency, per-step predicate rate; and at each checkpoint a fixed 40-case debug-seed (4097) evaluation of tail-predicate fraction and sustained success under the D-034 reducer. Report whether rising return accompanies stationary holding.

Evaluation: the final PPO policy and the frozen R-039 gait on fresh 30-case promotion manifests per stage (seeds 4030-4032), one evaluator process per (stage, controller), identical placements, frozen D-034 reducer; the R-039 amended reproducibility gate (zero outcome flips, <= 4/40 diverged envs) applied to the PPO cell on debug seed 4097 (3 stages x 40 cases x 2 processes).

Prediction per stage: paired_success_difference >= +0.10 vs the gait on 30 pairs; falsified by an upper paired bound below +0.10. Qualification >= 27/30 sustained per stage, independent of the comparison. Qualified checkpoints are exported with observation/action traces and provenance for trace repair.

Episode accounting: 1.08e9 transitions ~ 3.0e6 full-horizon episodes (actual completed episodes counted from resets, including early terminations), + 180 evaluation + 240 control + up to 10 x 40 checkpoint diagnostics on seed 4097; 0 LLM calls; wall time replaced by measured throughput after the gate.

falsified_by: Per stage: an upper paired interval bound below +0.10 rules out the predicted gain; an interval containing +0.10 is uncertainty, not improvement. Expert qualification fails at a stage below 27/30 sustained successes regardless of return.

history.note: pre-launch reconciliation (R-037 precedent): seeds 4020 (training), 4030-4032 (promotion manifests, frozen and committed) and 4097 (debug-only diagnostics/gate) reserved in the ledger before any promotion-case rollout, so protocol.seeds is empty and protocol.manifests names the frozen files. A smoke test of the full chain ran at 256 envs, 6 iterations, with 'promotion' manifests rebuilt from debug seed 4097 in /tmp, so no promotion case was opened. Runner setting: clip_actions = 1.0 so the observed last_action matches the evaluator's clamped action.

direction: Continue researching the single-step exploration pipeline with plateau-triggered trace repair, extended to pen spinning on the Shadow Hand (Isaac Lab Isaac-ShadowHandSpin-Stage{1,2,3}-Direct-v0, vendored in lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin; 157-d full obs, 20-d action, 60 Hz, 360-step episodes). Expert demonstrations: first try a hand-written scripted spinning controller; also search online for an existing trained pen-spinning policy; if neither qualifies, train an RL expert (rsl_rl PPO on the box). No budget ceiling on GPU hours or LLM calls. Known gaps to turn into questions: the env's spin_rate is roll about the pen's own long axis (not end-over-end twirl), success is per step with no episode rule, and the pipeline (manifests, obs schema, runner, records) is MetaWorld-only today. Debug issues, improve the pipeline, and turn unexpected findings into concrete research questions; document results and limitations.

advisor.reasoning: PPO is the appropriate fallback because the public-policy search is already negative, but R-039 must first identify unresolved stages and freeze the scripted comparator. The maximum 90,180 simulator episodes and zero LLM calls should not be committed before that gate; the new training entrypoint is justified because no inventoried script trains rsl_rl PPO. Its weakest point is that the initial training schedule is uncalibrated, so failure would establish failure of that schedule rather than impossibility of learning an expert.

implementer.reasoning: Agree on gating behind R-039. For re-triage: the budget is badly calibrated. 30000 episodes is about 10.8M env steps per stage at 256 envs, roughly two orders of magnitude below what Shadow Hand in-hand tasks usually need. Isaac Lab's cube repose defaults to 8192 envs and far longer training. The stage-1 reward also weights centring (3.0) far above spin (0.15), so PPO may learn to hold the pen still. The revision should budget in env steps with many more envs, log spin_rate and success separately from return, and treat a reward-shape check as part of the protocol.

advisor.reasoning: R-039 failed expert qualification on all three stages, so the prerequisite that justified deferral is now resolved and PPO is the prescribed next route. I accept the implementer's objection that 10.8 million transitions per stage is an inadequately calibrated dexterous-control budget, and that return must be separated from roll and sustained success. The reward coefficients motivate a diagnostic, but do not alone establish that holding still is optimal; the revised experiment should test the existing reward before changing it.
suggested_changes: Replace the unresolved-stage gate with execution on all three stages, using the frozen R-039 feedback gait as the comparator rather than the earlier oscillator. Keep training seeds 4020–4022 and fresh promotion seeds 4030–4032, which remain unspent.

Replace the 30,000-episode training cap with a predeclared schedule of up to 1.08 billion environment transitions per stage. Target 8192 parallel environments; validate memory and throughput during the initial training segment, then freeze the largest feasible batch size before continuing. Retain the declared stage-to-stage transfer and final-scheduled-checkpoint selection; do not use promotion outcomes to select checkpoints or extend training.

Update estimated cost to 3.24 billion training transitions plus at most 180 evaluation episodes, approximately 9,000,180 full-horizon-equivalent episodes and zero LLM calls. Estimate actual completed episodes from observed episode lengths, count every reset including setup and early terminations, and replace the unsupported 720-minute estimate with measured throughput.

Log return components, axial spin rate, end-over-end angular rate, fall frequency, tail-predicate fraction and sustained success separately at fixed training checkpoints. Record whether increasing return accompanies stationary holding; reward changes require a separately frozen follow-up rather than adaptation within this comparison.

Retain the prediction: paired_success_difference increases by at least 0.10 against the frozen R-039 gait, reported separately by stage on 30 fresh paired cases. State falsified_by as an upper paired interval bound below +0.10; otherwise report uncertainty rather than treating an interval containing zero as evidence of improvement. Expert qualification remains at least 27/30 sustained successes per stage, independently of whether the comparative prediction holds.

Reuse config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml, the vendored ShadowHandSpinPPORunnerCfg and the manifest-driven evaluator built in R-038/R-039. Add only the missing PPO training entrypoint; preserve the frozen no-fall, all-final-60-steps reducer, identical reset placements, one evaluator process per cell and the amended reproducibility gate established in R-039.

implementer.reasoning: Agree with revise and with changes 1, 4, 5 and 6: frozen R-039 gait as comparator, diagnostics logged separately from return, prediction +0.10 per stage with the stated falsifier, qualification at 27/30 under the frozen reducer, one new entrypoint reusing the vendored runner config and the R-039 evaluator and control gate. Amend changes 2-3: train ONE policy on Stage 3, not three. The three stages are one physics (the configs differ only in reward weights and success thresholds), and the per-step predicates nest: center_dist < 0.08 and |roll| > 4 implies < 0.10 and > 3 and > 1, so any Stage-3 sustained success is a sustained success at Stages 1 and 2 on the same trajectory (verified in R-039's offline multi-stage scoring). Evaluating the Stage-3 policy on all three stages' fresh promotion manifests answers the per-stage question at one third of the 3.24e9-transition cost, about 30+ T4 hours saved. It also removes the transfer-schedule choice, which is an uncalibrated free parameter. Schedule: up to 1.08e9 transitions, a throughput and memory gate in the first segment (8192 envs targeted; freeze the largest feasible batch before continuing), final scheduled checkpoint only, and fixed checkpoints every 10% for the diagnostics. If the Stage-3 policy fails a stage that a Stage-1 policy might pass, that is a follow-up with its own seeds, not an adaptation. Seeds: training 4020 (one run), promotion 4030-4032; 4021-4022 are released unused.

advisor.reasoning: I accept the implementer's single-Stage-3-policy argument: shared physics and nested predicates make evaluation across all three stages informative at one third of the proposed training cost, without an arbitrary transfer schedule. The scripted and public-policy routes are exhausted, so the roughly 3.01 million episode-equivalent budget and zero LLM calls are justified; reuse the existing config, vendored runner and manifest evaluator, adding only the missing PPO entrypoint. Its weakest point is one training seed on the hardest reward: failure would establish failure of this schedule, not that stage-specific PPO cannot qualify. Retain the per-stage prediction that paired_success_difference increases by at least 0.10 against the frozen R-039 gait; falsified_by is an upper paired interval bound below +0.10, while qualification independently requires 27/30 sustained successes and promotion requires a paired interval lower bound above zero.

implementer.reasoning: Agreed protocol: one Stage-3 PPO policy (seed 4020), up to 1.08e9 transitions with a first-segment throughput/memory gate, fixed 10% checkpoints for diagnostics only, final scheduled checkpoint evaluated on fresh per-stage promotion manifests (4030-4032) against the frozen R-039 gait, D-034 reducer, R-039 amended reproducibility gate on debug seed 4097. The advisor's caveat stands and will be in the record: one seed on the hardest reward tests this schedule, not PPO in general.
